# Tweak reference

Every tweak shipped in [`catalog/tweaks.json`](../catalog/tweaks.json) (catalog v1, updated 2026-09-16).

Each entry lists the exact commands it runs, what it needs, and how it is undone.
Nothing here requires root.

**Legend** — 🟢 low risk · 🟡 medium · 🔴 high · `settings` = works with the *modify system settings* access alone, no Shizuku · `shizuku` = the app needs Shizuku · `adb` = run the commands from a computer.

## Works without Shizuku

**8 of 39 tweaks never need the shell user.** They only touch the `system` namespace, which an ordinary app may write once you grant *Settings → Apps → Special access → Modify system settings*. That grant is a single toggle, so these work with no Shizuku, no root and no computer — this is the path to take if you would rather not install Shizuku at all.

- `force-max-refresh-rate` — Pins Android's peak and minimum refresh rate to the panel maximum, so every app — not just the whitelisted ones — runs at 120/144/165 Hz.
- `refresh-rate-overlay` — Enables the developer overlay that displays the current refresh rate in the corner of the screen — the honest way to check whether a tweak actually worked.
- `lock-rotation-portrait` — Disables the accelerometer auto-rotate and pins the display portrait. Great for reading in bed.
- `font-scale-compact` — Shrinks text 15 % to fit more rows of content on screen.
- `screen-timeout-30s` — Shortens the display timeout to 30 seconds.
- `disable-adaptive-brightness` — Stops the ambient-light-driven brightness hunting that keeps waking the sensor hub.
- `disable-touch-sounds` — Kills key-click, touch and screen-lock audio feedback.
- `disable-haptics` — Turns off UI vibration feedback. On iQOO's oversized linear motors this is a noticeable battery and comfort change.

## Details

### force-max-refresh-rate

**Force maximum refresh rate (120 / 144 / 165 Hz)** — 🟢 low risk · needs `settings` *(no Shizuku)* · verified on hardware

Pins Android's peak and minimum refresh rate to the panel maximum, so every app — not just the whitelisted ones — runs at 120/144/165 Hz.

OriginOS ships a per-app high-refresh whitelist. Apps that are not on it are silently clamped to 60/90 Hz even when the panel supports more. Writing `peak_refresh_rate` and `min_refresh_rate` in the `system` namespace overrides the clamp process-wide.

Side effects: 10–20 % extra battery drain, and a few video apps (Netflix, Prime Video) may lose frame-rate matching. Revert restores your previous values exactly, including the case where the key did not exist before.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos2`, `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`, `funtouch13`, `funtouch14`, `funtouch15`

- _read first:_ `adb shell settings get system peak_refresh_rate`
- `adb shell settings put system peak_refresh_rate 144.0`
- _read first:_ `adb shell settings get system min_refresh_rate`
- `adb shell settings put system min_refresh_rate 144.0`

**Revert:** the previous value is captured before the change and restored by `originos-toolkit revert` (or *Revert* in the app).

<sub>inverse=settings_put, inverse=settings_put</sub>

### dark-mode-always

**Force dark mode system-wide** — 🟢 low risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Sets UI mode to night regardless of the toggle in Quick Settings (useful to keep dark mode from losing to a schedule).

Uses `cmd uimode night yes`, the same command the Settings app uses internally. Revert runs `cmd uimode night no`; use the app's Auto option if you want the scheduler back.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos2`, `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`

- `adb shell cmd uimode night yes`

**Explicit revert:**
- `adb shell cmd uimode night no`

### animation-speed-fast

**Snappier UI (0.5× animations)** — 🟢 low risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Halves window, transition and animator durations. The cheapest perceived-performance win on any Android device.

This does not make the device faster, it makes it *feel* faster. Some OEM animations look slightly cut off at 0.5×; try `animation-speed-off` if you like it extreme.

**Revert:** the previous value is captured before the change and restored by `originos-toolkit revert` (or *Revert* in the app).

### animation-speed-off

**Kill all animations (0×)** — 🟡 medium risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

### density-compact

**Increase screen real estate (density −10 %)** — 🔴 high risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Lowers display density by 10 % so every app shows more content. Computed from your current density, never hard-coded.

Uses a *relative* delta: the engine reads `wm density`, applies −10 %, and journals the original value, so it is safe on any panel.

Risk: some apps with hard-coded layouts break at odd densities, and a wrong density used to be able to soft-lock the UI. That is why the revert journal is written **before** the change, and `Settings → Panic reset` always restores factory density with `wm density reset`.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos2`, `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`

- _read first:_ `adb shell wm density`
- `adb shell wm density 414`  _(computed from your real density)_

**Revert:** the previous value is captured before the change and restored by `originos-toolkit revert` (or *Revert* in the app).

### disable-window-blurs

**Disable window blurs (GPU win)** — 🟢 low risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Turns off the system-wide background blur effect. Free frames on OriginOS, which uses heavy blur in the notification shade and Control Center.

Set to `1` to disable. OriginOS's Control Center will look flat instead of frosted; that is the whole point. No effect on Android versions before blurs existed.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`

- _read first:_ `adb shell settings get global disable_window_blurs`
- `adb shell settings put global disable_window_blurs 1`

### max-cached-processes

**Keep more apps warm (cached processes ×2)** — 🟡 medium risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Raises the activity-manager cached-process allowance so apps relaunch instantly instead of cold-starting.

Writes the `activity_manager` device_config key. OriginOS's aggressive memory killer normally wins anyway on 8 GB devices; on 12 GB+ this measurably reduces relaunch cost.

Costs RAM headroom — if you see more background kills than before, revert. Needs a reboot to take full effect.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`

- _read first:_ `adb shell device_config get activity_manager max_cached_processes`
- `adb shell device_config put activity_manager max_cached_processes 64`

**Revert:** the previous value is captured before the change and restored by `originos-toolkit revert` (or *Revert* in the app).

<sub>inverse=device_config_put</sub>

### private-dns-adguard

**Private DNS with ad-blocking (DoT)** — 🟡 medium risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Routes all DNS through AdGuard's encrypted DNS-over-TLS resolver, killing most in-app ads network-wide — no VPN slot used, no root.

Writes the global `private_dns_mode=hostname` + `private_dns_specifier`. Because it runs in the network stack, it blocks ads inside every app including games, with zero battery cost from a local VPN.

Caveats: some captive portals and a few Chinese CDNs misbehave. If your network breaks, revert or switch the specifier to `one.one.one.one`. Requires a Wi-Fi/cellular reconnect to take effect.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos2`, `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`, `funtouch13`, `funtouch14`, `funtouch15`

- _read first:_ `adb shell settings get global private_dns_mode`
- `adb shell settings put global private_dns_mode hostname`
- _read first:_ `adb shell settings get global private_dns_specifier`
- `adb shell settings put global private_dns_specifier dns.adguard-dns.com`

**Revert:** the previous value is captured before the change and restored by `originos-toolkit revert` (or *Revert* in the app).

<sub>inverse=settings_put, inverse=settings_put</sub>

### debloat-vivo-store-browser

**Debloat: Vivo Store + Browser** — 🟡 medium risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Disables the Vivo App Store and the Vivo browser for the current user. Both are push-notification and background-network offenders.

Uses `pm disable-user --user 0`, which is fully reversible without reflashing and keeps the APKs on the read-only partition untouched.

You lose: App Store updates for Vivo system apps, and the default browser (install Chrome/Firefox first). OTA system updates use a separate updater package and keep working.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos2`, `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`, `funtouch13`, `funtouch14`, `funtouch15`

- _read first:_ `adb shell pm list packages -d com.vivo.appstore`
- `adb shell pm disable-user --user 0 com.vivo.appstore`
- _read first:_ `adb shell pm list packages -d com.vivo.browser`
- `adb shell pm disable-user --user 0 com.vivo.browser`

**Revert:** the previous value is captured before the change and restored by `originos-toolkit revert` (or *Revert* in the app).

### debloat-vivo-analytics

**Debloat: Vivo analytics & telemetry** — 🟡 medium risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Disables Vivo's A/B analytics collector. Commonly reported to cut idle wakeups and background traffic.

Targets `com.vivo.abe`. Nothing user-facing depends on it; on a minority of builds the *iManager* battery screen loses some statistics. Revert any time.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos2`, `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`

- _read first:_ `adb shell pm list packages -d com.vivo.abe`
- `adb shell pm disable-user --user 0 com.vivo.abe`

**Revert:** the previous value is captured before the change and restored by `originos-toolkit revert` (or *Revert* in the app).

### gesture-navigation

**Gesture navigation (no buttons)** — 🟡 medium risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Switches the navigation bar to gesture mode via the system overlay, restoring the 3-button bar on revert.

Uses the RRO overlays `navbar.gestural` / `navbar.threebutton`, which is exactly what the Settings toggle does. The explicit revert re-enables the three-button overlay, so you never end up with an invisible navbar.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos2`, `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`, `funtouch13`, `funtouch14`, `funtouch15`

- _read first:_ `adb shell cmd overlay list --user 0`
- `adb shell cmd overlay enable --user 0 com.android.internal.systemui.navbar.gestural`
- _read first:_ `adb shell cmd overlay list --user 0`
- `adb shell cmd overlay disable --user 0 com.android.internal.systemui.navbar.threebutton`

**Explicit revert:**
- `adb shell cmd overlay enable --user 0 com.android.internal.systemui.navbar.threebutton`
- `adb shell cmd overlay disable --user 0 com.android.internal.systemui.navbar.gestural`

### confirm-immersive-mode

**Skip immersive-mode confirmation dialogs** — 🟢 low risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Pre-confirms full-screen immersive mode so games do not pop "swipe up to exit full screen" the first time.

Writes `immersive_mode_confirmations=confirmed` in the secure namespace — the documented way for kiosk and gaming setups to suppress the prompt.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos2`, `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`

- _read first:_ `adb shell settings get secure immersive_mode_confirmations`
- `adb shell settings put secure immersive_mode_confirmations confirmed`

**Revert:** the previous value is captured before the change and restored by `originos-toolkit revert` (or *Revert* in the app).

<sub>inverse=settings_put</sub>

### enable-wireless-debugging

**Enable wireless debugging (self re-arm)** — 🟡 medium risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Flips the wireless-debugging flag so a restarting Shizuku or a fresh ADB session can reconnect without a computer.

Writes `adb_wifi_enabled=1`. This is a convenience flag: Android still asks for a pairing code the first time, and the port changes on every reboot. Read `docs/NO-ROOT-SETUP.md` for the full wireless-debugging recipe.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos2`, `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`, `funtouch13`, `funtouch14`, `funtouch15`

### trim-caches

**Trim caches now (free storage)** — 🟢 low risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Asks PackageManager to drop app caches. Frees space instantly; apps simply rebuild their caches.

One-shot maintenance action, not a state change, so it has no revert. `pm trim-caches` takes a free-space target; we pass 999G to mean "trim everything you safely can".

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos2`, `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`

- `adb shell pm trim-caches 999G`

**Revert:** not applicable — this is a one-shot action that does not change persistent state.

---

### kill-background-apps

**Kill all background apps** — 🟡 medium risk · needs `shizuku` · verified on hardware

Frees RAM right before you launch a heavy game.

Runs `am kill-all` — it only kills processes Android considers killable, so no foreground app is harmed. One-shot, no revert needed. OriginOS's own game launcher does the same thing.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos2`, `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`

- `adb shell am kill-all`

**Revert:** not applicable — this is a one-shot action that does not change persistent state.

### fixed-performance-mode

**Fixed performance mode (experimental)** — 🔴 high risk · needs `shizuku` · **community-submitted, unverified**

Pins the SoC to its maximum frequency instead of scaling. Benchmarks scream; the phone gets hot and the battery melts.

Runs `cmd power set-fixed-performance-mode-enabled true`. **Not verified on every OriginOS build** — it is a no-op on most OEM kernels and the command may return "Unknown command". True reverting requires `cmd power set-fixed-performance-mode-enabled false`; a reboot always clears it.

Do not leave it on for normal use. Thermal throttling still applies, so a long gaming session may end up *slower* than adaptive scaling.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`

- `adb shell cmd power set-fixed-performance-mode-enabled true`

**Explicit revert:**
- `adb shell cmd power set-fixed-performance-mode-enabled false`

---

### doze-force-idle

**Force Doze now (experimental)** — 🟡 medium risk · needs `shizuku` · **community-submitted, unverified**

Puts the device into deep idle immediately instead of waiting for the motion sensors to agree.

Runs `dumpsys deviceidle force-idle`. All background network activity stops within seconds, including notifications, until the screen is touched. Great for measuring true idle drain overnight. Not a persistent change.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`

- `adb shell dumpsys deviceidle force-idle`

**Revert:** not applicable — this is a one-shot action that does not change persistent state.

---

### record-fps-sample

**Sample the real frame rate (experimental)** — 🟢 low risk · needs `shizuku` · **community-submitted, unverified**

Dumps the SurfaceFlinger frame timeline so you can verify whether a game is really running at 144 Hz.

Runs `dumpsys SurfaceFlinger --latency` — the raw latency buffer for the system compositor layer. Output format differs between OriginOS builds and some builds restrict it without root, which is why this is flagged experimental. The app's own FPS overlay uses a Choreographer-based fallback when this returns nothing.

**OriginOS compatibility:** `originos2`, `originos3`, `originos4`, `originos5`, `originos6`

- `adb shell dumpsys SurfaceFlinger --latency`

**Revert:** not applicable — this is a one-shot action that does not change persistent state.
